chunks.arabic_text: وَسَأَلَهُ عَبْدُ الرَّحْمَنِ بْنُ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ:

translations.en: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Abī ʿAbdillāh asked him:

chunks.arabic_text: عَنْ رَجُلٍ أَعْتَقَ عَبْدًا لَهُ وَلِلْعَبْدِ مَالٌ فَتُوُفِّيَ الَّذِي أَعْتَقَ الْعَبْدَ لِمَنْ يَكُونُ مَالُ الْعَبْدِ أَيَكُونُ لِلَّذِي أَعْتَقَ الْعَبْدَ أَوْ لِلْعَبْدِ

translations.en: About a man who freed a slave of his, while the slave had wealth, then the one who freed the slave died. To whom does the slave's wealth belong? Does it belong to the one who freed the slave, or to the slave?

chunks.arabic_text: قَالَ إِذَا أَعْتَقَهُ وَهُوَ يَعْلَمُ أَنَّ لَهُ مَالًا فَمَالُهُ لَهُ وَإِنْ لَمْ يَعْلَمْ فَمَالُهُ لِوُلْدِ سَيِّدِهِ.

translations.en: He said: "If he freed him while knowing that he had wealth, then his wealth belongs to him. But if he did not know, then his wealth belongs to the children of his master."

en.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling regarding the wealth held by a slave at the time of manumission. If the master knowingly frees a slave who possesses wealth, that wealth remains with the freed slave; if the master was unaware of it, the wealth goes to the children of the former master. The narration addresses ownership, emancipation, and posthumous financial rights.
en.seo_question: When a slave is freed and has wealth, who owns that wealth according to this hadith?

key_terms.مَالٌ: property or wealth owned or possessed
key_terms.لِوُلْدِ سَيِّدِهِ: for the children of his master
